parameters.text:
=You are an expert resume analyst. Extract a clean, structured profile from the CV text below.

Respond ONLY with valid JSON — no markdown code fences, no commentary before or after. If a field is not present in the CV, use null (or an empty array for list fields). Escape any quotation marks inside string values with a backslash.

Schema to follow exactly:
{
  "name": "<candidate full name>",
  "currentRole": "<most recent job title>",
  "yearsExperience": <total years of relevant professional experience, as a number>,
  "field": "<primary professional field/industry, e.g. 'Software Engineering', 'Marketing', 'Finance'>",
  "primarySkills": ["<core skills the candidate is strongest in>"],
  "secondarySkills": ["<supporting/familiar skills>"],
  "education": "<highest relevant degree/institution>",
  "certifications": ["<any certifications>"],
  "expectedSalary": "<stated salary expectation if mentioned in the CV, else null>",
  "preferredLocation": "<stated location preference if mentioned, else null>",
  "remotePreference": "<'Remote' | 'Hybrid' | 'On-site' | null if not stated>",
  "summary": "<2-3 sentence honest summary of this candidate's overall career profile and strengths>"
}

CV_TEXT:
{{ $json.text }}

parameters.text:
=You are an expert technical recruiter and honest career advisor helping ONE candidate decide which jobs are worth applying to. You will be given TWO candidate CVs and one job posting. Compare them carefully and return a rigorous, honest assessment — do not be falsely encouraging, and do not inflate a score for a role that looks good on paper but has a structural blocker.

CV OPTION 1 — file "{{ $('Parse CV 1 Profile').first().json.fileName }}":
{{ JSON.stringify($('Parse CV 1 Profile').first().json) }}

CV OPTION 2 — file "{{ $('Parse CV 2 Profile').first().json.fileName }}":
{{ JSON.stringify($('Parse CV 2 Profile').first().json) }}

JOB_POSTING:
Title: {{ $json.title }}
Company: {{ $json.company }}
Location: {{ $json.location || "Not specified" }}
Remote: {{ $json.remote || "Not specified" }}
Posted Salary (if any): {{ $json.salary || "Not specified" }}
Description: {{ $json.description }}

TASK:
1. Read the full posting carefully: role, responsibilities, explicit requirements, location, and compensation (if listed).
2. Pick the better-fit CV for THIS job. As a rule: the CV named "Product" is written for PM/PO-facing roles (product management, product ownership, growth, roadmap ownership); the CV named "Tech" or "Delivery" is written for CTO/technical-leadership-facing roles (engineering leadership, delivery management, technical program roles). Base the final call on the actual job title AND full description, not just keyword overlap or the file-name rule alone. Run every step below against the CV you picked; ignore the other one from this point on.
3. Compare the chosen CV against the posting across FOUR dimensions:
   - Skills: do the specific tools, methodologies, and competencies the posting names actually appear in the CV's bullets — not just adjacent or implied?
   - Experience: does the candidate's actual work history (companies, roles, scope of what was really done) map to what's being asked?
   - Seniority: does the role's scope (IC vs. team lead vs. department head vs. C-level) match the candidate's actual level — not over- or under-qualified?
   - Industry: does the specific vertical (fintech, iGaming, travel, insurtech, banking, etc.) match something the candidate has actually worked in, or is it a name-only overlap with a different industry?
4. Classify every gap you find as Serious or Minor:
   - Serious = explicitly required, hard to fake or bridge quickly, likely to get the candidate filtered out early (missing industry experience, a required certification, a mandatory named tool/skill, wrong location/visa).
   - Minor = "nice to have," a softer skill, or something the candidate likely has but that just isn't visible on the CV.
5. Score fit from 0-100:
   - Hard, explicitly-stated requirements the candidate doesn't meet (required industry experience, mandatory certifications/tools, location/relocation/visa) drag the score down hard — often into skip territory — regardless of how well the softer skills match.
   - Missing "nice to have" items cost much less.
   - Strong overlap on core responsibilities and a proven track record pushes the score up.
   - Do NOT inflate the score for a role that looks good on paper but has a structural blocker (wrong location, wrong required industry, wrong seniority band).
6. Decide shouldApply as "Yes", "Maybe", or "No" using judgment, not the score alone. Example: a 55 score with strong domain fit and only Minor gaps can still be "Yes". A 75 score with one Serious blocking requirement can still be "No". As a loose guide, 60+ with no Serious gaps generally means "Yes"; a real Serious gap or a different-industry/wrong-seniority mismatch pushes it toward "No" regardless of score.
7. Salary recommendation: figure out whether this role is effectively a LOCAL Georgian-market role (Tbilisi-based, on-site or local hybrid) or an INTERNATIONAL/remote role (use the Remote field, Location, and how the company/description reads — an international remote-friendly company or fully remote posting counts as international). Then:
   - If LOCAL: recommend a realistic salary range using typical Georgian market rates for this role, seniority, and field, benchmarked against a Tbilisi-based candidate.
   - If INTERNATIONAL/remote: recommend a realistic salary range using typical international remote-role rates for this role, seniority, and field.
   - If the posting already states a salary, compare it against your benchmark and say whether it's below/at/above market.
   - Clearly state which benchmark you used, and explicitly flag that this is an estimate from general knowledge, not live market data.

Respond ONLY with valid JSON — no markdown code fences, no commentary before or after. Escape any quotation marks inside string values with a backslash.

Schema to follow exactly:
{
  "cvUsed": "<exact file name of the CV you picked in step 2, copied exactly from CV OPTION 1 or CV OPTION 2 above>",
  "cvChoiceReasoning": "<1 sentence: why this CV (Product vs Tech & Delivery) fit better than the other for this specific role>",
  "rank": <integer 0-100, per the scoring rules in step 5>,
  "shouldApply": "Yes" | "Maybe" | "No",
  "domainMatch": "Same domain" | "Adjacent/transferable" | "Different domain",
  "whyFit": "<Start with the ONE line that matters most for the shouldApply verdict, then 1-2 more sentences covering how Skills/Experience/Seniority/Industry fit compared>",
  "blockingGaps": "<Serious gaps only — explicitly required, hard to bridge, likely to filter the candidate out early. 'None' if there are none.>",
  "learnableGaps": "<Minor gaps only — nice-to-have, soft skill, or something likely present but not visible on the CV. 'None' if there are none.>",
  "salaryRecommendation": "<recommended range with currency, e.g. '3500-5000 GEL/month' or '$70k-$90k/year'>",
  "salaryReasoning": "<1-2 sentences: which benchmark (Tbilisi/Georgian local vs international remote) you used and why, explicitly noted as an estimate>"
}
